question: Should OpenClaw add `sandbox.docker.env.*` to the supported SecretRef credential surface even though resolved values still become Docker environment variables visible through Docker metadata?
rationale: The source change is a bounded implementation path, but accepting a new credential surface in Docker env is a security-boundary and product-policy choice that automation should not settle.

options.title: Accept the guarded SecretRef surface
options.body: Proceed with the linked PR after maintainer/security review confirms the docs warning and Docker metadata exposure are acceptable for this config-time credential surface.

options.title: Keep docker env string-only
options.body: Reject the feature and continue steering operators to custom images, mounted secret files, or other delivery paths when Docker metadata exposure is not acceptable.

options.title: Defer to per-call injection design
options.body: Leave this config-time request open or close it only after a broader operator-trusted per-call env design such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/80329 is selected.

recommendation.title: Accept the guarded SecretRef surface
recommendation.body: Proceed with the linked PR after maintainer/security review confirms the docs warning and Docker metadata exposure are acceptable for this config-time credential surface.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has direct history on sandbox env sanitization and the remaining blocker is the security boundary rather than implementation mechanics.
